free_tier.stated: Quick Transfers are free and have NO file-size limit, but they are ephemeral P2P: 'deleted automatically when either party closes the transfer window'. Persistent storage starts at Starter $6/mo (200 GB storage, 200 GB/file, 14 days).

retention.stated: until the instance is recycled; not persistent

egress.terms: free for Quick Transfer (browser-to-browser, so their egress is minimal).

record.tooling: Open source (github.com/robinkarlberg/transfer.zip-web, 1,514 stars) and self-hostable. Which means you can run the whole service on your own box, but that is your storage, not theirs.
record.chaining: The free path is a WebRTC pipe, so it multiplies to nothing durable. Self-hosting it is a legitimate option only if you already have the disk.
record.limits_note: per-object-cap: none on Quick Transfer, 200 GB on Starter. Retention: zero on Quick Transfer (session-bound); 14 days on Starter paid. 'Unlimited free file size' on the marketing page refers to the P2P mode.
record.reliability_note: Its own terms are unambiguous that Quick Transfers are ephemeral and that paid plans are a pool of SIMULTANEOUS storage, not cumulative. Reading 'unlimited free file size' as a storage quota would be a mistake.

evidence.proved: 'Quick Transfers are ephemeral and are deleted automatically when either party closes the transfer window'
Starter $6/mo: Max file size 200 GB, expiry 14 days, storage 200 GB
